summary: A strong, well-reasoned spec that improved on the periphery this round — it fixed the model set to exactly four working roles with validated vendor invariants (orchestrator model explicitly outside the set), it now mechanically enforces the symbol up-link via an elegant L4 inheritance rule, it added the clearest idempotency reasoning in the field (idempotencyKey plus a state-guarded resend predicate that names and closes the running-but-turnSeq-unincremented race), and it added a spec_digest integrity check that escalates SPEC_MUTATED at phase boundaries. But it left its central defect intact for a third round: canComplete() requires every VerificationRecord to have git_rev==head_rev and status==pass, while records auto-stale when git_rev!=HEAD and the tester writes the record during E2E — so committing the record mutates HEAD and self-stales it, making DONE unreachable as literally specified. It also performs the final decision-log→§A migration and spec retirement as unreviewed DONE side-effects, contradicting its own doc-only-requires-re-review rule, and its committed reviewer lens split routes correctness/security review primarily to the same-family reviewer. Its orchestrator-compaction handling (budget + escalate-at-boundary + disk state) is reasonable but, unlike proposal-1, cannot detect a silent early compaction. Adoptable, but the completion criterion must be repaired first — the fix (adopt proposal-1's parent-revision metadata commit) is small.

blocking_findings.description: The completion criterion is self-contradictory and possibly unreachable: canComplete() requires VerificationRecord git_rev==head_rev ∧ status==pass, but records auto-stale on git_rev!=HEAD and are written+committed during E2E, so persisting the record advances HEAD and staled it. The doc-only-doesn't-invalidate-E2E claim also cannot reach DONE without re-running E2E on the doc-inclusive head. Persisted three rounds despite being flagged each time.
blocking_findings.required_change: Adopt proposal-1's guarded metadata-only verification commit recording the parent executable revision, and define canComplete() over that parent (or a code-tree hash) rather than a HEAD the verification write itself mutates.

blocking_findings.description: Final decision-log→§A migration and tracked-spec retirement run as terminal DONE effects after canComplete() is checked, so the final committed tree is never reviewed or E2E'd — and this contradicts proposal-2's own rule that doc-only commits require a cheap knowledge re-review.
blocking_findings.required_change: Move the §A migration and spec retirement into execution (as proposal-1 does) so the attested revision is the final knowledge state, or run a mandatory re-review of the finalization diff before declaring DONE.

blocking_findings.description: The committed reviewer lens split assigns correctness/security to the same-family reviewer and business/architecture to the cross-vendor one, reducing independent cross-vendor coverage of the bug classes most likely to be model-family-correlated.
blocking_findings.required_change: Keep both reviewers on the full unified rubric with lens as advisory emphasis only.

non_blocking_findings.description: Budget + escalate-at-boundary + disk-persisted state is reasonable, but there is no detection of an unexpected silent compaction, so a degraded orchestrator could keep making decisions unnoticed (which proposal-1's contextEpoch catches).

assumptions: verification-state.json is a tracked file under docs/knowledge/, so writing it is a tracked change subject to the completion invariant.
The four-role model set and orchestrator-model separation now fully satisfy the 'модели четырёх ролей' constraint.
The L4 up-link inheritance rule (implicit when a module maps to exactly one §A) is an acceptable mechanical reading of 'linter checks the necessary reference'.
